steps.tx: **Sepsis-3** defines sepsis as life threatening organ dysfunction from a dysregulated host response, recognised as infection plus an acute **SOFA** rise of at least 2 points. **SIRS** is not the definition. Systemic inflammatory response criteria lack specificity and occur in non-infectious insults, whereas an acute shift in SOFA reflects measurable physiological organ failure.

steps.tx: **Septic shock** is a vasopressor requirement to keep mean arterial pressure at least 65 mmHg plus a **lactate** above 2 mmol/L despite adequate fluid. Either finding alone is not the definition. Combining persistent vasopressor dependence with cellular metabolic distress identifies a distinct subset with hospital mortality exceeding forty percent.

rows: Maintain MAP at or above 65 mmHg

steps.tx: **qSOFA** is a bedside prompt outside the ICU, not a diagnostic criterion. A low qSOFA does not exclude sepsis. Counting respiratory rate of 22 or more, systolic blood pressure of 100 mmHg or less, and altered mentation identifies ward patients at elevated risk of deterioration without requiring laboratory tests.

left.title: qSOFA bedside tool
points: Includes altered mentation with GCS under 15
Includes systolic blood pressure 100 mmHg or less

right.title: Clinical positioning
points: Positive score warrants immediate SOFA assessment

steps.tx: Endothelial **glycocalyx injury** increases permeability, so fluid leaves the vessels and the patient becomes oedematous while still intravascularly depleted early on. Shedding of syndecan and heparan sulphate disrupts vascular barrier integrity, causing massive transcapillary albumin flux and profound third-space tissue oedema.

rows: Loss of vascular charge barrier and permeability leak
Profound arterial vasoplegia refractory to catecholamines
Heterogeneous capillary flow and functional shunting

steps.tx: Later sepsis includes **immunoparalysis**, with falling monocyte **HLA-DR** and secondary infection. More immunosuppression is not the treatment of that phase. Lymphocyte apoptosis and immune checkpoint upregulation leave prolonged ICU survivors vulnerable to opportunistic viral reactivation, invasive fungal infections, and hospital-acquired multidrug-resistant pathogens.

left.title: Initial hyperinflammation
points: Tissue collateral damage and early shock

right.title: Secondary immunoparalysis
points: Profound depletion of CD4 and dendritic cells
Marked suppression of monocyte HLA-DR expression
High susceptibility to secondary nosocomial sepsis

steps.tx: **Sepsis induced coagulopathy** is a distinct score from overt DIC. **Thrombocytopenia** and a rising INR in sepsis are a reason to look for DIC, not an automatic plasma transfusion. Prophylactic transfusion of clotting factors without active haemorrhage or planned invasive procedures exposes patients to transfusion-related acute lung injury without improving survival.

rows: Treat underlying sepsis; initiate heparin prophylaxis
Serial laboratory tracking; avoid empiric plasma

steps.tx: A **cytokine storm** is the phenotype of some viral and **CAR-T** illnesses. Ordinary bacterial sepsis is not treated with cytokine blockade outside a specific indication such as COVID-19. Targeting individual inflammatory mediators with monoclonal antibodies in unselected bacterial sepsis repeatedly failed to demonstrate clinical survival benefits in large multicentre trials.

left.title: Targeted cytokine release syndrome
points: Triggered by CAR-T cells or severe viral pneumonia
Massive systemic interleukin-6 and interferon surge
Responds dramatically to targeted tocilizumab blockade

right.title: Bacterial sepsis pathogenesis
points: Broad poly-microbial and complex immune cascade
Anti-TNF and anti-IL-1 therapies proved ineffective

steps.tx: **Mitochondrial dysfunction** is one reason lactate stays high after perfusion has been restored. It is not fixed by another litre of fluid. Cytopathic hypoxia and inhibition of pyruvate dehydrogenase prevent normal aerobic respiration, so loading additional volume merely accelerates fluid overload without improving cellular bioenergetic ATP production.
